label: Tax collector
summary: The character who is the tax collector of this tax slot.
details: Works on a tax slot and leads to a character.

label: Tax slot
summary: The tax slot this character collects taxes for.
details: Works on a character who is a tax collector. The result is the slot of which they are the collector.

label: Tax slot liege
summary: The liege of this tax slot.
details: Works on a tax slot and leads to a character. Vanilla does not use it, and the game does not say more about who exactly counts as the liege here.

label: Tenet
summary: The tenet with the given key.
details: Written `tenet:<key>`, where the key is the name of a tenet. Works anywhere, from any starting point.

label: This
summary: The thing the script is currently working on, unchanged.
details: Use it when you need to name the current thing itself, for example to pass it on or compare it with something else. It does not move to another scope.

label: Holy order title
summary: The title that belongs to this holy order.
details: Works on a holy order and leads to its landed title.

label: Title by key
summary: The landed title with the given key.
details: Written `title:<key>`, for example `title:k_france`. Works anywhere, from any starting point.

label: Capital county of the title
summary: The title's capital county.
details: If the title is landless playable and has a holder, it gives the county of the holder's location instead. Otherwise it gives the title's preferred capital county.

label: Domicile of the title
summary: The domicile that goes with this title.
details: Works on a title and leads to a domicile. The title may have none, in which case there is nothing to continue with.

label: Preferred capital county
summary: The county the title prefers as its capital.
details: Works on a title and leads to a title. Unlike `title_capital_county`, the game's documentation does not mention the landless special case.

label: Title province
summary: The province of this title.
details: Works on a title and leads to a province. Vanilla uses it very often.

label: Top liege
summary: The top liege of this character, the one at the head of their liege chain.
details: Works on a character and leads to a character.

label: Top overlord
summary: The top overlord of this character, counting both liege and suzerain relationships.
details: Works on a character and leads to a character. The game's documentation names both liege and suzerain as overlords it counts.

label: Top participant group
summary: The participant group of a situation that this character belongs to, for the situation's top sub-region.
details: Written `top_participant_group:<situation>`, where the key names the situation. Works on a character and leads to a situation participant group.

label: Top religious superior
summary: The head of the character's faith.
details: Works on a character. Not every faith has a head, so there may be nothing there. Vanilla does not use it.

label: Top suzerain
summary: The top suzerain of this character.
details: Works on a character and leads to a character. It is separate from `top_liege` and `top_overlord`; the game's documentation does not say more about how the chain is followed.

label: Trait by key
summary: The trait with the given key.
details: Written `trait:<key>`, for example `trait:brave`. Works anywhere, from any starting point.

label: Travel leader
summary: The character who leads this travel plan.
details: Works on a travel plan and leads to a character.

label: Travel plan activity
summary: The activity tied to this travel plan.
details: A travel plan may have no activity, so the result can be empty.

label: Travel plan owner
summary: The character who owns this travel plan.
details: Works on a travel plan and leads to a character.

label: Number
summary: A plain number written directly, such as 1, 5.2 or -6.
details: Written `value:<number>`. Accepts any number, including negative and decimal ones. Works anywhere.

label: Variable
summary: A variable that was set earlier, looked up by its name.
details: Written `var:<name>`, for example `var:mortal_enemy`. It gives back what was stored under that name.

label: Vassal contract by key
summary: The vassal contract with the given key.
details: Written `vassal_contract:<key>`, where the key names a vassal contract. Works anywhere. Vanilla uses it only twice.

label: Contract of the obligation
summary: The vassal contract that this obligation level belongs to.
details: Works on a vassal contract obligation level and leads to a vassal contract.

label: Vassal's tax collector
summary: The tax collector of this character.
details: Works on a character and leads to a character. Vanilla does not use it, and the game's documentation is short, so who exactly counts as the collector here is not clear.

label: War
summary: The war of this casus belli.
details: Works on a casus belli and leads to a war.

label: Warden
summary: The character who holds this hostage.
details: Works on a hostage. If the character is not a hostage, the result is empty.

label: Yes
summary: The value true.
details: A fixed yes that can be used where a true/false value is expected. Works anywhere.
